info.name: Dexcom (aifitnessapi.com)
info.description: Dexcom: OAuth 2.0 requests built from the vendor documentation aifitnessapi.com quotes. Generated by scripts/build-collections.mjs; no secrets included. https://aifitnessapi.com/collections

item.name: OAuth 2.0
item.description:
Dexcom's authorization-code flow as its documentation describes it, read 2026-11-05. Fill client_id, redirect_uri and scope in an environment of your own and keep client_secret there, never in a shared collection.

The same facts, with each source sentence, at https://aifitnessapi.com/integrate/dexcom-api and https://aifitnessapi.com/tools/oauth-playground.

request.description:
https://api.dexcom.com/v3/oauth2/login. Login URL for the US production environment; the sandbox replaces the base URL with https://sandbox-api.dexcom.com. Open this URL in a browser (in Postman: copy it from the request bar); the user signs in and Dexcom redirects to {{redirect_uri}} with ?code=… Put that value in the auth_code variable.

Source: Dexcom Developer Portal, “Authentication”, https://developer.dexcom.com/docs/dexcom/authentication

Scope: One scope only: offline_access, always sent. Source: Dexcom Developer Portal, “Authentication”, https://developer.dexcom.com/docs/dexcom/authentication

Required scope: offline_access (the scope variable starts with it).

PKCE: Not mentioned. Dexcom also requires tokens and the client secret to live on your server, not on a phone.

Also documented: https://sandbox-api.dexcom.com/v3/oauth2/login. Sandbox login (no password; a drop-down of sandbox users). Source: Dexcom Developer Portal, “Authentication”, https://developer.dexcom.com/docs/dexcom/authentication

https://api.dexcom.com/v3/oauth2/token. Token URL (US production), form-encoded, for the exchange and refresh.

Source: Dexcom Developer Portal, “Authentication”, https://developer.dexcom.com/docs/dexcom/authentication

Client credentials go in the form body.

Token lifetime: expires_in is in seconds; Dexcom's sample response shows 7200 (two hours). Source: Dexcom Developer Portal, “Authentication”, https://developer.dexcom.com/docs/dexcom/authentication

Note: The authorization code is single-use and expires after one minute. Source: Dexcom Developer Portal, “Authentication”, https://developer.dexcom.com/docs/dexcom/authentication

Note: Tokens and the client secret must be stored on your servers, never on the mobile device. Source: Dexcom Developer Portal, “Authentication”, https://developer.dexcom.com/docs/dexcom/authentication

Note: A refresh token is valid for at most one year. Source: Dexcom Developer Portal, “Authentication”, https://developer.dexcom.com/docs/dexcom/authentication

Refresh: Each refresh token works once and is replaced by a new one; each lasts at most a year. A 400 on refresh means it is no longer valid: send the user through login again.

Source: Dexcom Developer Portal, “Authentication”, https://developer.dexcom.com/docs/dexcom/authentication

variable.description: Your app's client ID, from the vendor's developer console.
Keep it in a Postman or Bruno environment marked secret. This collection ships it empty.
The redirect URI registered with the vendor.
Scopes to request, joined as the vendor documents (see the authorization request).
A random value you check on the redirect.
The refresh_token from the token response.
